claims.locator: Swiss Ephemeris Programmer's Documentation sections 3, 5.8 and 12.2 for calc_ut, sidereal flags and ayanamsa modes; representative date checks in tests/test_drik_engine.py and tests/test_ayanamsa.py
claims.scope: Traces the Drik longitude API and preserves representative outputs. The current register does not contain an exhaustive independently published position-and-transition fixture, and it establishes no interpretive doctrine.

claims.locator: Chapter I verses 29-34 and 53 for revolution counts and mean place; chapter II verses 29-39 for anomaly, epicycle dimensions and the manda equation
claims.scope: Supports the mean-motion and manda-correction algorithm family and the Sun/Moon revolution and epicycle constants. The implementation uses direct floating-point trigonometry, a fixed code epoch and simplified apogee treatment; this claim does not make it a complete textual transcription or independently verify its modern Panchangam outputs.

claims.locator: _VAKYA_CORRECTIONS and _VAKYA_CYCLE_DAYS; research gap tracked in GitHub issue 176
claims.scope: The current nine-value offset over 3,031-day steps is regression-pinned but has no registered primary-table derivation or published-Vakya comparison set. It must be described as provisional, not as a verified 248-day or 248-year Vākya algorithm.

claims.locator: Swiss Ephemeris Programmer's Documentation sections 8.12 and 8.12.1; convention decision and comparison gap tracked in GitHub issue 177
claims.scope: Precisely traces the current astronomical-default rise_trans behavior: upper limb with refraction, fixed 1013.25 hPa and 15 C, and zero-metre altitude passed by all engines. It does not establish that this is the intended Hindu-calendar convention or independently verify multiple city/date cells.

claims.locator: 1 DP_VERIFIED cell; 29 ENGINE_PINNED cells in the fixture
claims.scope: Only cells marked DP_VERIFIED are independently verified.

claims.locator: tests/test_surya_siddhanta_engine.py and tests/test_vakya_engine.py
claims.scope: Regression tests preserve the current Surya Siddhanta and Vakya Pancha-Anga and sky-event outputs. No independent published-Panchangam comparison set is registered, so engine-pinned output must not be described as externally verified.

Samvatsara, Ayana, Ritu, lunar-month, Paksha, weekday and Rasi labels combine astronomical calculations with calendar rollover conventions. They require criterion-level locators and regional-scope notes; astronomical correctness alone does not verify the naming convention.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter III, Nakshatra Tyajyakala table, inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 7 (physical PDF p. 10), and Chapter V section 7, Durmuhurta, internal printed p. 13 (physical PDF p. 16); regional tables remain regression-pinned
claims.scope: The auspicious, inauspicious and Choghadiya response objects are mixed containers. Raman supports the four-Ghati Nakshatra Tyajyakala concept and his printed Durmuhurta scheme, but the project's regional weekday tables are not identical to Raman's table and the remaining Brahma Muhurta, Abhijit, Amrita Kalam, Rahu Kalam, Gulika, Yamagandam and Choghadiya components do not yet have criterion-level textual claims. This state records partial evidence, not umbrella verification.

claims.locator: Section 'About Abhijit Muhurat': the second paragraph defines Abhijit as the eighth of 15 equal sunrise-to-sunset parts; the following example derives 11:40-12:20 for a 06:00-18:00 day; the final paragraph records the Wednesday exclusion
claims.scope: Supports the maintained daylight-division formula and selected Wednesday convention. It is a published-Panchangam reference rather than a primary textual edition. The repository currently has one explicit location/date comparison for the displayed window, so this does not establish exhaustive multi-city output verification or universal activity suitability.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter V section 2, 'Surya Sankramana,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed pp. 12-13 (physical PDF pp. 15-16); the exact 16-Ghati rule is on internal printed p. 13 (physical PDF p. 16)
claims.scope: Supports rejecting sixteen Ghatis before and after Surya enters a new Rasi for new work. The implementation scales a Ghati to the local sunrise-to-next-sunrise Panchangam day. It does not implement any sign-specific longer Sankramana interval.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter III, 'Panchak (5-source energy),' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed pp. 8-9 (physical PDF pp. 11-12)
claims.scope: Supports adding the ordinal Tithi, weekday, Nakshatra and Lagna and reducing modulo nine; remainders 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 as Mrityu, Agni, Raja, Chora and Roga; and activity-specific avoidance for occupation, building, travel, marriage and Upanayanam. The broader software avoid-for aliases are operational mappings of those categories, not additional textual quotations.

claims.locator: tests/test_eclipses.py
claims.scope: The eclipse event pipeline is regression-tested against Swiss Ephemeris calculations. The ledger does not yet contain an independent event-by-event comparison fixture, so this is engine-pinned rather than externally verified.

Special Yogas, Panchaka labels, Khara month, Pitru Paksha, Simha-Stha, Maudhya, Anandadi Yoga, Disha Shoola, Nakshatra Mukha and Panchaka Rahita are separate traditional classifications. The group exists to expose evidence debt and grants no umbrella textual authority; each component needs its own inspected rule table and regional boundary.

claims.locator: Chapter CIV (104), stanza 4, including its concluding all-planets 11th-house statement
claims.scope: Supports the configured favourable houses counted from Janma Chandra for Surya, Chandra, Mangala, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani. The explicit houses in stanza 4 combine with its concluding statement that all Grahas are benefic in the 11th. It does not support the Vedha table, father-son exemptions, Rahu/Ketu convention, named Shani conditions, or the binary reduction of each transit to one verdict.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, slokas 3-8 (printed pp. 287-289); Jataka Parijata, Volume III, Adhyaya XIII, note to sloka 60, printed pp. 833-834 (PDF pp. 127-128)
claims.scope: Supports every configured favourable-house-to-Vedha-house pair for Surya, Chandra, Kuja, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani, plus the Surya-Shani and Chandra-Budha exemptions. It does not support this project's Rahu/Ketu policy or named Shani conditions. Brihat Samhita Chapter 104 is not the authority for this layer.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, sloka 2 (printed p. 286), especially the concluding direction that Rahu and Ketu are similar to Surya
claims.scope: Implements Phaladeepika 26.2's direction to treat Rahu and Ketu like Surya by admitting houses 3, 6, 10 and 11 from Janma Chandra. The passage does not establish whether nodes cause or receive Vedha, so the separate no-node-Vedha policy remains an explicitly unverified conservative boundary and does not inherit authority from this locator.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, sloka 1 for Janma Chandra as the transit reference and slokas 22-23 (printed pp. 295-296) for Shani's effects in houses 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12
claims.scope: Verifies that these five Shani positions are reckoned from the natal Moon and have adverse classical transit effects. It does not verify grouping houses 12, 1 and 2 under the vernacular name Sade Sati; the names Ashtama Shani and Ardhastama Shani; the rising, peak and setting phase labels; or the deterministic advice sentences. Those remain configured conventional or project-interpreted presentation layers.

The generator verifies the rasi set and every declared graha, house and verdict in transits_cited against computed gochara. The text and advice fields are model interpretation: they are screened for unsupported precision and selected high-stakes directions but are not semantically or scripturally verified. They must never inherit the authority state of their cited transit triples.
Each activity needs rule-level locators; shared defaults must not imply universal textual agreement.

claims.locator: ACTIVITY_RULES['any']; shared scoring pipeline in personal/muhurta.py
claims.scope: The 'Anything auspicious' selector deliberately adds no activity-specific rule. It exposes the finder's shared Panchanga, Choghadiya, Lagna, personal-strength and relative-tier calculations as a source-neutral exploratory ranking. It is not a classical election for an unspecified act, must not be described as scripturally verified, and should yield to every purpose-specific profile when the intended act is known.

claims.locator: PROJECT_HEURISTIC_FIELDS in tools/export_muhurtam_rule_crosswalk.py; matching ACTIVITY_RULES fields and personal/muhurta.py scorer branches
claims.scope: Criterion-level project rules that have no registered source locator, including shared special-Yoga, Adhika, Khara-Maasa, Pitru-Paksha and Simha-Stha safeguards; selected Choghadiya, Tithi-family, Lagna-class, Nakshatra-Mukha and Vishti choices; and explicitly disclaimed vehicle, gold, purchase, travel, pilgrimage and surgery fields. These predicates may be useful conservative filters or ranking signals, but they do not inherit textual authority from the surrounding activity profile.

claims.locator: score bonuses and penalties in personal/muhurta.py; post-screen tie-breaks, unresolved-review caps and result-tier caps in src/scorer/election-chart-enrichment.ts
claims.scope: Owns product policy for numeric weights, tie-break ordering, relative result tiers and unresolved-review caps. A cited source may support preferring or rejecting a criterion, but it does not thereby authorize the app's +1/-1/configured weight, ranking order or Excellent/Good label.

claims.locator: manual rows whose display_section is practical, plus purchase.manual-3 and expert-profile practical disclosures in tools/export_muhurtam_rule_crosswalk.py
claims.scope: Product safety, scope-routing and real-world override disclosures. These statements keep medical care, legal duties, consent, financial judgment, ritual authority and physical safety ahead of electional timing, and route users to narrower activity profiles. They are product policy even when a row also paraphrases source context.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter IX, 'Electing a time for marriage,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed pp. 41-42 (physical PDF pp. 45-46), from the lunar-month paragraph through the election-chart conditions
claims.scope: Supports six unconditionally admitted lunar months plus the Pushya/Makara and Chaitra/Mesha exceptions; exact rejection-derived Tithi admissions; Tuesday exclusion with four best and two middling weekdays; eleven Nakshatras; nine computable named Nitya-Yoga exclusions; Vishti rejection; three best and five middling rising Rasis; and the six visible chart prerequisites. The Drik website post-screen now deterministically requires a vacant 7th house, Mangala outside the 8th and Shukra outside the 6th across every sampled state (window edges and both sides of every known interior Drik Lagna transition); remaining chart fortification, compatibility, Pada and non-Nitya Mrityu-Yoga clauses stay manual. Adhika, Pitru Paksha, Sankramana, combustion and Simha-Stha filters are separately disclosed conservative Panchanga-Shuddhi safeguards rather than being attributed to this passage.

claims.locator: Drik Panchang, 2026 Hindu Marriage Dates for Hyderabad and Panchang Shuddhi methodology; reviewed 2026-07-22
claims.scope: The published Hyderabad table admits qualifying Tuesdays and includes Tithis such as Chaturdashi, Pournami, Shashthi and Navami that Raman's method rejects. It also applies solar/lunar month, Adhika, Chaturmas and Guru/Shukra Asta filters. This is a real lineage and methodology divergence: the product follows its explicitly named Raman profile, preserves separately sourced conservative safeguards, and does not claim identity with Drik Panchang's marriage-date set.

claims.locator: Vivaha-prakarana, 'Kanyavarana Muhurta' and 'Varavarana (Phaladana) Muhurta,' verses 10-11, printed pp. 103-104 (Internet Archive OCR lines 5337-5360); marriage-star expansion referenced by verse 10 is verse 55, printed pp. 125-126 (OCR lines 6401-6426)
claims.scope: For a mutual engagement, implements the intersection of both sides' directly stated Nakshatra admissions: Rohini, Krittika, the three Purvas and the three Uttaras. Verse 10 admits Kanyavarana under nine named stars or the marriage-election stars in verse 55; verse 11 admits Varavarana/Phaladana under Rohini, all three Uttaras, Krittika and all three Purvas. Every verse-11 star is also admitted by verse 10, so the eight-star intersection is exact. Verse 11 additionally says Shubha day, Tithi and Lagna without enumerating them in this passage; those remain mandatory practitioner prerequisites. This profile governs mutual ritual selection/gift exchange, not relationship compatibility or the wedding ceremony.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter XII, 'House building,' section 'Entering a new house,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed pp. 52-54 (physical PDF pp. 56-58)
claims.scope: Supports the exact Monday/Wednesday/Thursday/Friday gate; Krishna Pratipat and the seven named Shukla Tithis; the five best plus two permissible Nakshatras; Surya in the six traditional Uttarayana Rasis; fixed Rasi preference with dual Rasis admitted as ordinary; and conservative omission of the movable-Rasi/Vrishabha-Navamsa exception. The Drik website post-screen now requires a vacant 8th house across every sampled state (window edges and both sides of every known interior Drik Lagna transition) and can use one selected householder's natal Nakshatra, Rasi or Lagna match as a non-inflating preference. Graha strength, other house placements, Navamsa, ritual preparation and the advanced-pregnancy restriction remain visible manual prerequisites. The scope is first entry into a newly built home, not purchase, rental moving or post-repair re-entry.

claims.locator: Drik Panchang, 2026 Griha Pravesh Dates for Pune, methodology and date table; reviewed 2026-07-22
claims.scope: The published Panchang Shuddhi practice rejects Sunday and Tuesday but admits qualifying Saturdays, while Raman's named auspicious list is Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday and reports Saturday only as another-writers' view with a theft caution. Drik Panchang also applies lunar-month and Adhika-month filters beyond this Raman profile. The product follows its named Raman lineage and discloses rather than merges this current-practice divergence.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter XVII, 'Miscellaneous elections,' section 'Filing law-suits,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 67 (physical PDF p. 71)
claims.scope: Supports rejection of Tuesday and Saturday; admission of Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Anuradha, Dhanishtha and Revati; Mesha Lagna or the manual alternative of Mesha Navamsa; Guru in a Trikona from a strengthened Lagna; no malefic in the 6th; and separation of the Lagna and 6th lords. The passage says to avoid the usual unfavorable lunar days without repeating them; automation transparently resolves that phrase to Raman's recurring explicit list in the same inspected derivative: Chaturthi, Shashthi, Ashtami, Navami, Dwadashi, Chaturdashi, Pournami and Amavasya. The profile is limited to filing or initiating a lawsuit and does not cover hearings, responses, settlement, appeals or outcome prediction. Legal obligations always take precedence. The legacy litigation API key resolves explicitly to this profile and is not a separate election.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter XVII, 'Miscellaneous elections,' section 'Filing law-suits,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 67 (physical PDF p. 71)
claims.scope: Historical audit of the removed standalone Litigation / contest profile. It preferred Mangalavaram although Raman rejects Tuesday and Saturday for filing lawsuits, added unsupported Jaya/Purna family scoring, and attached an activity-specific Bhadra Puchha bonus without a located passage. The public litigation key is now only a compatibility alias for the corrected, narrowly scoped court filing profile; this contradicted claim is retained as the correction record, not as an active activity claim.

claims.locator: Shubhashubha-prakarana, verses 43-45, printed pp. 20-21 (Internet Archive OCR lines 1743-1797)
claims.scope: Implements verse 44's Tithi-specific Yama assignments for all eight Vishti-bearing Tithis. The equivalent four-quarter form places Mukha in quarter 1/2/3/4 for Shukla Chaturthi/Ashtami/Ekadashi/Pournami and the paired reverse-order Krishna Tithis, with Puchha in quarter 4/1/2/3 respectively. Mukha occupies five nominal Ghatis and Puchha three; both are scaled from the verse's nominal thirty-Ghati Vishti measure to the observed Karana duration. Verse 45's Bhadra-residence classification is not inferred from these sub-windows.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Pretakriya ka muhurta,' verse 48, printed pp. 47-48 (OCR lines 2956-2971 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Implements the verse's nine-star positive admission list for Pretakriya that could not be performed at the time of death: Ashvini, Pushya, Hasta, Ashlesha, Moola, Jyeshtha, Shravana, Ardra and Swati. This narrower deferred-rite scope removes the former generic Antyeshti ranking and does not require approximating the separate four-and-a-half-Nakshatra cremation prohibition, because none of Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada or Revati is admitted by the positive list. Immediate legal, medical and ritual duties override the finder; the profile must never be used to delay Antyeshti.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Homahuti Muhurta' and 'Agnivasa,' verses 35-36, printed pp. 43-44 (OCR lines 2773-2796 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Implements both conjunctive tests in verses 35-36 as hard gates. Homahuti counts the Moon's Nakshatra inclusively from Surya's Nakshatra in nine successive groups of three, assigned to Surya, Budha, Shukra, Shani, Chandra, Mangala, Guru, Rahu and Ketu; groups of the natural benefics Budha, Shukra, Chandra and Guru are admitted. Agnivasa numbers Tithis 1-30 from Shukla Pratipat and weekdays 1-7 from Sunday, adds one to the Tithi count, and admits modulo-four remainders 3 or 0, which place Agni on earth. The activity is deliberately scoped to a Homa offering (Homahuti), not every Yajna; rite-specific Kalpa and Sampradaya requirements remain manual.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter X, 'Lending Money,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 45 (physical PDF p. 49)
claims.scope: Supports hard exclusion of Krittika, Magha, Moola, Shatabhisha, Uttara Phalguni, Punarvasu and the lender's Janma Nakshatra; Tuesday/Friday exclusion; and the exact Saturday-Amavasya conditional prohibition. Lagna/7th-lord harmony and Chandra outside Vrischika remain manual checks. This is lender-side guidance only and cannot establish creditworthiness, repayment, enforceability or investment safety.

claims.locator: Drik Panchang, Loan Giving Muhurat methodology, example page for 11 June 2026, Chincholi, Karnataka; reviewed 2026-07-22
claims.scope: The published methodology says not to give a loan on Wednesday, directly differing from Raman's Tuesday-and-Friday exclusion and implicit Wednesday admission. The configured profile follows the explicitly named Raman lineage and discloses, rather than merges, this current-practice divergence.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter X, 'Borrowing Money,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 45 (physical PDF p. 49)
claims.scope: Supports hard exclusion of Krittika, Moola, Punarvasu, Dhanishtha and each borrower's Janma Nakshatra. Chandra-Mangala/Shani conjunction and purpose-specific Chandra relationships remain manual checks. It supplies no weekday, Tithi, Lagna-class or Choghadiya preference. This is debtor-side election guidance only; repayment capacity, borrowing cost, collateral, lender terms and professional advice take precedence.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Dravyaprayoga and taking a loan,' verse 27, printed pp. 38-39 (OCR lines 2578-2599)
claims.scope: The inspected commentary joins debt-taking to a broader Dravyaprayoga/capital-deployment election with twelve named Nakshatras, Chara Lagna, benefics in the 5th/9th and an empty 8th. It does not reproduce Raman's Krittika/Moola/Punarvasu/Dhanishtha/Janma exclusion set. This is a disclosed lineage/scope divergence, not authority to merge the formulas.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter X, 'Buying for Business,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 45 (physical PDF p. 49); Muhurta Chintamani, Nakshatra-prakarana, purchase/sale distinction, verse 16, printed pp. 33-34 (OCR lines 2336-2350)
claims.scope: Raman supports Thursday, Dashami and Pushya as independent preferences, complete rejection of Tuesday, Saturday as passable, and the disclosed Budha/2nd-house/Mangala/Guru chart checks. Muhurta Chintamani independently supports the buyer-versus-seller boundary, not Raman's inventory formula. This is for purchasing stock, raw materials or goods for resale/business use, not selling inventory, launching an enterprise or deploying capital. Commercial, cash-flow, tax and legal judgment take precedence.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, purchase/sale distinction and purchase Muhurta, verse 16, printed pp. 33-34 (OCR lines 2336-2350); marketplace election, verse 17, printed pp. 34-35 (OCR lines 2351-2374)
claims.scope: Verse 16 supports the configured preference for Revati, Shatabhisha, Ashvini, Swati, Shravana and Chitra from the buyer's perspective. Verse 17 supports the disclosed marketplace checks: reject Rikta Tithis, Tuesday and Kumbha Lagna; place Chandra and Shukra in Lagna, keep malefics out of the 8th and 12th, and place benefics in the 2nd, 10th or 11th. The Drik website post-screen now treats Chandra-in-Lagna and Shukra-in-Lagna as source preferences only when they pass across every sampled state (window edges and both sides of every known interior Drik Lagna transition); the remaining marketplace house placements stay manual. The Labh-Choghadiya bonus is a separate project heuristic, not authorized by these verses. Object-specific vehicle, building-land and jewelry profiles remain narrower authorities and take precedence.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Entering the service of a master,' verse 26, printed p. 38 (OCR lines 2565-2577); 'Sandhana Muhurta,' verse 42, printed pp. 45-46 (OCR lines 2880-2891)
claims.scope: Supports the employee-side act of entering service under seven named Nakshatras and Wednesday, Friday, Sunday or Thursday, with a benefic in Lagna, Surya or Mangala in the 10th/11th, employer/employee birth-Nakshatra Yoni friendship and friendship between their Janma-Rasi lords. The weekday and star gates are automated; the Drik website post-screen now treats Surya-or-Mangala in the 10th/11th as a preference only when it passes across every sampled state (window edges and both sides of every known interior Drik Lagna transition). Benefic Lagna strength and two-person compatibility remain mandatory practitioner checks. This does not cover offer acceptance, modern contract signing, incorporation or hiring staff. Employment terms, labour law and workplace safety take precedence. The former Amrit, Nanda and Sthira-Lagna proxies have been removed.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Dravyaprayoga and taking a loan,' verse 27, printed pp. 38-39 (OCR lines 2578-2599); compare marketplace verse 17, printed pp. 34-35
claims.scope: Supports twelve named Nakshatras, Chara Lagna, benefics in the 5th and 9th houses and an unoccupied 8th for Dravyaprayoga: putting funds to work, including investing capital in employment or business. The Chara requirement is automated; the three house conditions remain mandatory practitioner checks. This does not authorize a universal company-founding election and excludes marketplace opening, inventory purchase and lending, which are separate activities. Commercial, legal and financial judgment always takes precedence. The former Amrit, Nanda, weekday and Sthira-Lagna proxies have been removed.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Shantika and Paushtika Muhurta,' verse 34, printed pp. 42-43 (OCR lines 2749-2772 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Supports the exact rejection of Rikta Tithis, Ashtami, Pournami and Amavasya; admission of Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; fifteen named Nakshatras; and rejection of Sankramana. The Drik website post-screen now treats Surya in the 10th, Chandra in the 4th and Guru in Lagna as source preferences only when they pass across every sampled state (window edges and both sides of every known interior Drik Lagna transition). Combustion, exceptional omens and the remedial Shanti urgency exception remain manual. The profile is limited to Shantika rites that pacify affliction and Paushtika welfare rites, including the passage's Puja, Purashcharana and Mula-shanti examples; it is not a universal ceremony election.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, Dharma-kriya commencement in verse 30, printed pp. 40-41 (OCR lines 2685-2700 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Supports the thirteen named Nakshatras; Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; Budha- or Guru-ruled Lagna or Varga; Guru in Lagna; and adequate personal Guru-bala. Automation conservatively admits the four Budha/Guru-ruled Lagnas, while the Varga alternative, Guru occupation and personal Guru strength remain mandatory practitioner checks. The scope is beginning Dharma-kriya—religious or meritorious work—not every modern project, habit, relationship, relocation or life change. The former Amrit Choghadiya and Nanda-Tithi proxies have been removed because verse 30 does not supply them.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter XII, 'House Building' / 'Laying the Foundation,' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed pp. 50-51 (physical PDF pp. 54-55)
claims.scope: Supports the configured house-foundation lunar-month, Tithi-number, Nakshatra, weekday, solar-Rasi and fixed-Lagna criteria. Full election-chart house occupancy/aspects and ritual site placement are disclosed manual checks. Shared samskara filters, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: B. V. Raman, Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Naming the child (Namakarana),' inspected in the 2020 Chistabo derivative at internal printed p. 22 (physical PDF p. 25)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Namakarana weekday and Nakshatra admission lists, rejected Tithi numbers, fixed-Lagna preference, timing-after-birth guidance and disclosed election-chart/name checks.
